I wonder if people see being party to cheating better than, the same as, or worse than cheating.

Explanations of your thoughts would be great too.
What do you think of people who knowingly have sex with someone who's in a monogamous relationship?
I mean, morally suspect at least. They clearly don't have much respect for others.

It's not socially acceptable, however, it generally isn't as bad as cheating: they didn't enter into a contract of monogamy.

I say "generally", because if they deliberately go out of their way to seduce a person in a relationship, then I feel it is worse. It didn't 'just happen', as such.
Why is deliberately seducing someone in a relationship bad? The seducer isn't the one who made a commitment.
Why is stealing bad? The thief isn't the one who has a contract with the object (purchase).

It's as bad as cheating. It's like aiding and abetting. If one party knowingly initiates and pursues the relationship more than the other party, then they're worse, but both are close to equally guilty in my book.

eh, if the cheater initiated everything then I don't care at all.

if the person went out of their way to convince someone to cheat then it's kinda a dick move and not someone I'd hang with.

The blame rests solely with the cheater...

Is it in bad taste to pursue someone in a monogamous relationship? Yes, but at the end of the day it's the cheater choosing to break the social contract.

We're all adults and enter into contracts both social and otherwise. If we choose to violate said contract it's our bad not the other party. The other party has no obligation to enforce a contract that exists between two other individuals. (The cheater and the one who's been cheated on)

If the cheater is unhappy with their current social contract (monogamy), what ever the circumstances. It's their responsibility to attempt try and work things out or realize that it's too far gone or an unhealthy relationship and end it. You are responsible for your own happiness... No one else.

You could argue entrapment as a possible defense for the cheater but again this also brings into question the fact entrapment is between officer(s) and an individual which the officers have contract to up hold law... Also most places still have the motto "To protect & Serve" and the other party has no such contract.

You can make all sorts of rationalizations. "Obviously the other person isn't serious about their relationship." "Likely that person will cheat one way or another"- not necessarily true, but an easy rationalization to make. "I'm not responsible for the other person's decisions".

IMO, though, it's a scummy thing to do.

First, I ultimately do think it's none of my direct business. I can have opinions on it, and I can maybe even raise an eyebrow, but I'm only accountable for my life, so I try to be somewhat reserved in my opinions of other people's lives.

Having said that, I do think that they are setting themselves up for unhappiness. Think about it: If you actually succeed in pulling someone away from their wife/husband/SO, then all you get is a lover who you know cheats. If you don't "win" over the existing partner, you're getting involved in a relationship with no future. Either way, it is hard for me to imagine very many affairs genuinely do end in happiness, although perhaps they sometimes do.

But maybe neither the cheater nor the cheatee want a "real" relationship and would prefer the casual thrill of clandestine sex. That still betrays someone's trust and carries certain risks (including the loss of a meaningful relationship), but people are in charge of making their own choices.
